title.narrative: Provision of Essential GBV Response Services and Strengthening Community-Based Protection Mechanisms in Kassala and Al Jazeera States

description.narrative: ltpgtThe ongoing crisis in Sudan, particularly in Al Jazirah, has created extreme protection risks, significantly increasing the vulnerabilities of women, girls, boys, and men. The collapse of governance structures, security systems, and social services due to conflict has forced families to flee their homes. Many now live in overcrowded, under-resourced displacement sites where living conditions are dire and the threat of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) is pervasive. Women and girls face heightened risks of harassment, assault, rape, intimate partner violence (IPV), and other forms of GBV. These concerns have been confirmed by the GBV Area of Responsibility (GBV AoR), with survivors and stakeholders reporting severe gaps in protection services, psychosocial support, and access to essential items needed for dignity and safety.ltbrgtThis multi-sectoral project responds to these urgent needs by integrating GBV prevention and response, Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ES/NFI), and Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA). It targets 54,092 people across Kassala and Al Jazirah States, including IDPs, refugees, returnees, and vulnerable host community members. The intervention will be delivered in Al Girba, New Halfa, Reifi Kassala, Kassala and Atbara River - Refi Nahar Atbara (Kassala), and Managil and Qurashi (Al Jazirah).ltbrgtThe GBV component reaches 35,450 individuals with life-saving, survivor-centered services. Five Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) will be established across both states, offering GBV case management, psychosocial support (PSS), referrals, and life skills training. Through these spaces, 1,250 individuals will receive structured case management and PSS, while 18550 dignity kits will be distributed to vulnerable women and girls.ltbrgtCommunity-Based Protection Networks (CBPNs) will be formed and trained to identify, refer, and respond to GBV cases, lead awareness efforts, and promote safe access to services. Awareness sessions will reach 16,650 individuals, including 150 adolescent girls. GBV safety audits will be conducted to identify risks and inform mitigation strategies.ltbrgtAlight will implement the protection component in Al Jazirah in partnership with NADA (Nada Elazhar for Disaster Prevention and Sustainable Development), a national NGO. NADA will lead protection activities in Managil and Qurashi, ensuring local relevance, better community engagement, and strengthened coordination with local authorities. Their involvement supports sustainability, enhances national capacity, and ensures delivery is culturally appropriate.ltbrgtThe ES/NFI component will support 1,140 vulnerable households with emergency shelter kits and 1,515 vulnerable households with essential shelter Non food items including blankets, mosquito nets, and solar lamps, improving safety and dignity in informal settlements. MPCA will support 1,200 households with cash assistance to meet basic needs, reducing reliance on harmful coping strategies such as transactional sex or child marriage.ltbrgtTo ensure accountability and adaptiveness, the project integrates strong monitoring and community feedback mechanisms including hotlines, suggestion boxes, and consultations. These tools will promote inclusivity, ensure services meet community needs, and support evidence-based program management.ltbrgtlt/pgt
